content.value_statement: Backend test coverage is hard to keep consistent across routes, services, models, and middleware. This skill detects project patterns and helps generate practical Jest, Supertest, and MongoDB tests.
actual_capabilities: Detects Jest, Vitest, or Mocha from package.json before generating tests.
Chooses unit or integration testing based on backend file type.
Provides setup and teardown guidance for MongoDB Memory Server tests.
Supplies test patterns for routes, services, models, middleware, and utilities.
Covers success, validation, auth, not found, duplicate, and edge cases.
Reports generated test files, total cases, and the next test command.
limitations: Targets MERN and Node backends; other stacks need adaptation.
Requires source files to be read before useful tests can be generated.
May require user approval to add missing test dependencies.
Generated tests still need execution in the local project.

use_cases.title: Add Missing API Tests
use_cases.description: Generate route and controller tests that cover status codes, validation, auth, and duplicate records.

use_cases.title: Standardize Test Setup
use_cases.description: Create consistent Jest, Supertest, and MongoDB Memory Server setup across a Node project.

use_cases.title: Review Release Coverage
use_cases.description: Find backend test gaps before release and prioritize missing cases by impact.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Backend Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one backend file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to generate tests for src/routes/users.routes.js. Follow the project test framework and include setup notes.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Route Integration Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for HTTP behavior coverage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill on src/routes/users.routes.js. Include success, validation, auth, not found, and duplicate cases.

prompt_templates.title: Build Service Unit Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill for src/services/user.service.js. Mock repository and email dependencies. Cover duplicate, failure, and success paths.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Test Coverage Gaps
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request across multiple backend layers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill across routes, middleware, and models. Identify existing test gaps, generate priority labels, and propose helper factories.

output_examples.input: A user route file with create, update, and delete handlers.
output: An integration test plan for each route and expected status code.
Generated cases for validation errors, auth failures, missing records, and duplicate users.
A short summary with test count and the command to run next.

output_examples.input: A service module with repository and email dependencies.
output: A unit test suite plan using mocked collaborators.
Cases for successful creation, duplicate email, repository failure, and email failure.
Notes about which dependencies are mocked and why.

output_examples.input: A project without a configured test framework.
output: An infrastructure checklist for Jest, Supertest, and MongoDB Memory Server.
A prompt to confirm dependency setup before any installation steps.
Guidance for placing setup files and test fixtures.

best_practices: Read target source and existing tests before generating new files.
Keep integration tests isolated with database setup and cleanup.
Run the local test command after generation and fix failures promptly.
anti_patterns: Starting a live server when Supertest can import the app.
Committing generated tests before checking secrets, fixtures, and cleanup.

faq.question: Which backend stacks does this skill support best?
faq.answer: It works best with MERN and Node projects using Express, MongoDB, Jest, and Supertest.

faq.question: Can it create both unit and integration tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It chooses the approach from the file type and accepts user overrides.

faq.question: Does it install test dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: No. It checks for missing dependencies and should ask before setup changes.

faq.question: Does it replace existing tests?
faq.answer: No. It should inspect existing tests first and add missing coverage.

faq.question: Can it test protected routes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for valid tokens, invalid tokens, and missing auth headers.

faq.question: What should users do after generation?
faq.answer: Run the local test command, review failures, and adjust fixtures for project-specific behavior.
